```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, fig.align = "center",
  fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.2, dpi = 150,
  message = FALSE, warning = FALSE
)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(targets); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2) })
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 15))

# Every number in this deck is read from the {targets} store of rjkdc-analysis/;
# nothing is retyped except the papers' printed values we compare against.
store <- "../../_targets"
tr <- function(name) tar_read_raw(name, store = store)
for (f in list.files("../../R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
rc <- tr("revenue_chain"); pf <- tr("pareto_fit"); t8 <- tr("income_tax_table8")
t9 <- tr("npv_table9"); t10 <- tr("npv_table10"); mcs <- tr("npv_mc_ssrn"); mcn <- tr("npv_mc_nber")
nc <- tr("nber_ceiling"); ncol <- tr("nber_collectible"); hl <- tr("site_headlines")
outputs <- read.csv("../../export/r/outputs.csv"); inputs <- read.csv("../../export/r/inputs.csv")
ss <- formals(compute_npv_mc_ssrn); nb <- formals(compute_npv_mc_nber)
num <- function(x, d = 1) { s <- formatC(abs(x), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","); ifelse(x < 0, paste0("&minus;", s), s) }
h <- function(v, q, col = "reproduced") hl[[col]][hl$version == v & hl$quantity == q]
out <- function(id, col = "value") outputs[[col]][outputs$output_id == id]
dials <- site_dials(rc)
mm_lines <- sub("^## ", "", grep("^## [0-9]+\\.", readLines("../../MISMATCHES.md"), value = TRUE))
```

name: part-claim
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 1: The claim

---

# What is being estimated

**Proposition 40** taxes, once, 5% of the net worth of billionaires who lived in California on
1 January 2026 (payable over five years). Its proponents estimate it at about 100 bn. (Amounts in this deck are in billions of dollars, "bn".)

The RJKDC analysis asks a different question: **is the state better off, counting what it loses?**

$$NPV = WT - f \cdot \frac{C}{r}$$

.pull-left[

- $WT$: wealth tax collected, **once**
- $C$: income tax the billionaires pay, **per year**
- $f$: share of that income tax that leaves the state
- $r$: discount rate; $C/r$ is a stream of $C$ **for ever**, valued today

]

.pull-right[

.highlight-box[
The whole argument is a race between a one-time sum and a perpetuity. At $r$ = 1.5%, losing
one dollar a year for ever costs as much as losing `r num(1/0.015, 0)` dollars today.
]

]

---

# Two versions, side by side

.pull-left[

**SSRN 6340778**, 17 March 2026<br>
Rauh, Jaros, Kearney, Doran, Cosso

.big[`r num(h("ssrn","mc_mean_npv","printed"))` bn]
mean NPV; `r h("ssrn","mc_pct_negative","printed")`% of outcomes negative<br>
revenue "approximately `r h("ssrn","revenue_headline","printed")` billion"

Reproduced: `r num(mcs$summary$mean, 2)` (seeded run), `r num(tr("npv_mc_ssrn_analytic_mean"), 3)` (exact)

]

.pull-right[

**NBER c15504**, 22 September 2026<br>
Jaros and Rauh, litigation-weighted

.big[`r num(h("nber","mc_mean_npv","printed"))` bn]
mean NPV; `r h("nber","mc_pct_negative","printed")`% of outcomes negative<br>
revenue "approximately 30 billion" (`r h("nber","revenue_range_low","printed")` bn to `r h("nber","revenue_range_high","printed")` bn)

Reproduced: `r num(mcn$summary$mean, 2)` (seeded run), `r num(tr("npv_mc_nber_analytic_mean"), 2)` (exact)

]

.blue-box[
The project fixed, before seeing results, that the RJKDC side is shown as these **two** estimates
side by side: the SSRN anchor, and the NBER revision that changes mainly one input, litigation risk.
]

---
name: part-revenue
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 2: The revenue

---

# From 94 bn to about 40 bn (Sec 4)

```{r revchain, fig.height=3.6}
d <- data.frame(
  step = c("No one leaves\n(4.1)", "6 confirmed\ndepartures (4.2)", "10 departures\n(4.3)",
           "Swiss semi-elasticity\n10.32 (4.4)", "Preferred\n(4.5, printed)"),
  v = c(rc$baseline_precise, rc$confirmed6_ceiling, rc$expanded10_estimate, rc$literature_calibrated,
        h("ssrn","revenue_headline","printed")))
d$step <- factor(d$step, levels = d$step)
ggplot(d, aes(step, v)) + geom_col(fill = c(rep("#1f6fce", 4), "#eb6834"), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", v)), vjust = -0.4, size = 5) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "$B") + ylim(0, 105)
```

.small[
Each step sums 5% of each stayer's net worth, minus their home. The first four bars come out of the
authors' workbook to the cent. The fifth is a judgement: a semi-elasticity of 12 to 13 "plausible and
conservative" (p.14), giving 35-46 bn. Nothing in the code computes the 40 bn.
]

---

# The semi-elasticity: a 5-point tax, how much base leaves?

$$\varepsilon = \frac{\%\Delta\,\text{base}}{\Delta\,\text{rate (points)}}$$

.pull-left[

- **Observed, 6 departures:** base falls `r num(100*(1 - rc$confirmed6_ceiling/rc$baseline_literal), 1)`%,
  so $\varepsilon$ = `r num(100*(1 - rc$confirmed6_ceiling/rc$baseline_literal)/5, 2)`
- **Observed, 10 departures:** $\varepsilon$ = `r num(100*(1 - rc$expanded10_estimate/rc$baseline_literal)/5, 2)`
- **Swiss literature** (Brülhart et al. 2022): 0.24 × 43 = `r inputs$value[inputs$input_id=="brulhart_semi_elasticity"]`,
  so `r num(100*rc$migration_share, 1)`% of the base leaves

]

.pull-right[

.highlight-box[
Two things to argue with: the Swiss estimate comes from a **recurring** tax, applied here to a
**one-time** one; and it is applied linearly (10.32 × 5), steeper than the log form the NBER
revision later uses.
]

]

---
name: part-income
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 3: The income tax

---
name: income-tax-c

# How much do billionaires pay each year? (Sec 5.1)

.pull-left[

**Upper bound.** Fit a Pareto tail to the Franchise Tax Board's (FTB, the state tax agency) filer counts above 1M to 10M dollars of income:
$\hat\alpha$ = `r num(pf$alpha, 2)`. If the 212 billionaires *are* the 212 highest earners, they pay
**`r num(t8$mean_fy25[t8$K == 212], 2)` bn** a year.

**But** wealth is not income: many billionaires realise little in a given year. So place them at random
among the top $K$ filers.

]

.pull-right[

```{r table8, fig.width=5.6, fig.height=3.6}
ggplot(t8, aes(K, mean_fy25)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05_fy25, ymax = p95_fy25), fill = "#1f6fce", alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(colour = "#1f6fce", linewidth = 1) + geom_point(colour = "#1f6fce") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 500, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "pool size K", y = "$B per year") + theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

]

.highlight-box[
The authors call $K \approx 500$ "a reasonable lower bound": `r num(t8$mean_fy25[t8$K == 500], 2)` bn.
So $C \in [3.3, 5.8]$: a range between a model's upper bound and a **judgement** about the floor.
]

---
name: part-forever
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 4: For ever

---
name: perpetuity

# The perpetuity multiplier (Sec 5.2)

```{r mult, fig.height=3.2}
r <- seq(0.01, 0.06, by = 0.0005)
ggplot(data.frame(r, m = 1 / r), aes(100 * r, m)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "#eb6834") +
  annotate("point", x = c(1.5, 3, 4.5), y = 1 / c(0.015, 0.03, 0.045), size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = c(1.5, 3, 4.5), y = 1 / c(0.015, 0.03, 0.045) + 9,
           label = sprintf("%.0f", 1 / c(0.015, 0.03, 0.045)), size = 5) +
  labs(x = "rate, %", y = "$ today per $1 a year for ever")
```

.small[
The paper's text says the lost stream grows, so the rate should be $r - g$, and anchors it at 1.5%
(the S&P dividend yield). The Monte Carlo then draws its rate r from 1.5% to 4.5% and divides by it
directly. Same numbers, two meanings ([mismatches 2 and 3](../materials.html#mismatches)).
Whether the loss lasts **for ever** or about five years is the main objection of the [BSZ side](../../../bsz-analysis/site/) (Boll, Saez
and Zucman, who support the measure).
]

---

# Table 9: three scenarios, three rates

```{r t9tab, results="asis"}
w <- t9 %>% mutate(cell = paste0(num(npv), " <span style='color:#6b7682'>(PV lost ", num(pv_lost), ")</span>")) %>%
  select(label, r, cell) %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = r, values_from = cell)
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Scenario</th><th>1.5%</th><th>3.0%</th><th>4.5%</th></tr>')
for (i in seq_len(nrow(w))) cat(sprintf("<tr><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>", w$label[i], w[[2]][i], w[[3]][i], w[[4]][i]))
cat("</table>")
```

.small[
NPV in bn; every cell matches the printed Table 9 (p.19). Departure share $f = 1 - WT/94.2$: the income
tax lost is assumed proportional to the wealth lost.
]

.highlight-box[
The central scenario's 42.0 bn has no derivation anywhere ([mismatch 8](../materials.html#mismatches)).
And the headline `r num(h("ssrn","mc_mean_npv","printed"))` is **not** in this table: the central cell at
1.5% is `r num(t9$npv[t9$scenario=="central" & t9$r==0.015])`.
]

---
name: break-even

# The break-even departure share (Sec 5.4)

$$NPV = 0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x^* = \frac{WT \cdot r}{C}$$

If less than $x^*$ of the income tax base leaves, the tax pays for itself.

```{r t10tab, results="asis"}
w <- t10 %>% mutate(cell = paste0(num(100 * break_even_pct), "%")) %>% select(label, r, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = r, values_from = cell)
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Scenario</th><th>1.5%</th><th>3.0%</th><th>4.5%</th></tr>')
for (i in seq_len(nrow(w))) cat(sprintf("<tr><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>", w$label[i], w[[2]][i], w[[3]][i], w[[4]][i]))
cat("</table>")
```

.small[
At the authors' preferred revenue about 55% has left, above most thresholds. The paper calls this
its preferred revenue; the 55% is $1 - 42/94.2$, using Table 9's central scenario (42) rather than
the 'about 40' headline, so it inherits the proportionality assumption.
]

---
name: part-mc
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 5: The headline

---

# The Monte Carlo behind `r num(h("ssrn","mc_mean_npv","printed"))` (Sec 5.5)

.pull-left[

Draw 100,000 times, independently:

- revenue $WT \sim U[35, 67.51]$
- income tax $C \sim U[3.3, 5.8]$
- rate $r \sim U[0.015, 0.045]$
- departure share $f = 1 - WT/94.2$

.small[
The paper prints 67.1: a typo for 67.51 ([mismatch 1](../materials.html#mismatches)).
The revenue draw has mean `r num(h("ssrn","mc_expected_revenue"), 2)` bn, **above** the preferred 40 bn.
]

]

.pull-right[

```{r hist, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=3.2}
ggplot(data.frame(npv = mcs$draws$npv), aes(npv, fill = npv < 0)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(mcs$draws$npv), linetype = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#eb6834", `FALSE` = "#1f6fce"), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-250, 70)) + labs(x = "NPV, $B", y = "draws") + theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

]

.blue-box[
The draws are independent, so the mean has a closed form: `r num(tr("npv_mc_ssrn_analytic_mean"), 3)`,
which rounds to the printed value. The seeded run gives `r num(mcs$summary$mean, 2)`
([mismatch 9](../materials.html#mismatches)). The explorer shows the exact expectation for every setting.
]

---
name: part-nber
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 6: The NBER revision

---

# What the September version changes

.small[
1. **Base grown 7%** to 31 Dec 2026, rebuilt person by person (`final.csv`): `r num(nc$domestic_total_grown, 2)` bn face value.
2. **Seven confirmed departures** (adds Kalanick): ceiling `r num(nc$ceiling_recomputed, 2)` bn from the data; the script
   hard-codes `r nb$wt_max` ([mismatch 4](../materials.html#mismatches)).
3. **Litigation discount:** $E[R] = q \times R_{\text{recognized}}$ = `r ncol$q` × `r num(ncol$recognized, 2)` bn =
   **`r num(ncol$central, 2)` bn**. $q$ = 0.50 is borrowed from an accounting rule (ASC 740-10).
4. **Departure share drawn on its own:** $f \sim U[`r nb$f_min`, `r nb$f_max`]$.
5. **Revenue drawn from zero:** $WT \sim U[0, `r nb$wt_max`]$, mean `r num(h("nber","mc_expected_revenue"), 0)` = 0.5 × 72.
]

.highlight-box[
The code never multiplies by $q$. Its only trace is the zero lower bound ([mismatch 5](../materials.html#mismatches)):
a uniform draw from 0 has the same **mean** as a coin flip on 72, not the same distribution.
Lost income tax is **not** scaled by $q$: people who left do not come back if the Act is struck down.
]

---
name: part-argue
class: center, middle, inverse

# Part 7: What to argue about

---
name: seven-inputs

# The seven inputs that move the answer

```{r origins, results="asis"}
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Input</th><th>Values in the explorer</th><th>Origin</th></tr>')
for (d in dials) cat(sprintf("<tr><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td><span class='og %s'>%s</span></td></tr>",
  d$label, paste(d$labels, collapse = "; "), d$origin, d$origin))
cat("</table>")
```

.highlight-box[
`r sum(vapply(dials, function(d) d$origin == "guesswork", TRUE))` of the `r length(dials)` are guesswork.
The data (Forbes, FTB, the Pareto fit) set the scale; the sign is decided by the guesses.
[Try them in the explorer](../explorer/).
]

---

# Nine mismatches between text, READMEs and code

.small[
```{r mm, results="asis"}
cat(paste0(mm_lines, collapse = "\n"))
```
]

.blue-box[
We reproduce the code as shipped and record each discrepancy rather than fix it. Full text on the
[materials page](../materials.html#mismatches); every one is pinned by a test.
]
